subject: OptiMed POC: intermittent 503s during burst - bridge & triage playbook
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@optimed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: OptiMed Platform Team <infra@optimed.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T15:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood POC - intermittent 503s during high-concurrency tests

Hi Marissa,

Quick follow-up from our run this morning: during a 200-concurrency burst we saw ~7% 503s for generation calls (model: rdx-large-v1) between 15:10-15:13 UTC. The errors appear to correlate with requests that included long system prompts and enabled streaming.

I attached the trimmed logs (optimed_poc-logs-20270612.zip) and a short repro curl snippet. Can you advise the recommended escalation path? We’re on a tight deadline for the demo on Friday and need a reliable mitigation.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform, OptiMed

--- Attachment: optimed_poc-logs-20270612.zip (log bundle, 4 files, ~2.1MB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@optimed.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood POC - intermittent 503s during high-concurrency tests

Hi Elena — thanks for the logs, very helpful.

Quick notes from my side:
- We will stand up a short triage bridge with Runtime & SDK owners. Karthik (field eng) and Dev (runtime) are looped.
- Initial hypothesis: streaming + long system prompt => memory/kv cache pressure causing transient rejection under heavy batching.
- Short-term mitigation to try now: 1) disable streaming for the demo calls, 2) reduce per-request sequence length by truncating non-essential system content, 3) pin to the rdx-medium-v1 variant which has lower peak memory usage.

Can Karthik and Dev confirm availability for an urgent bridge in 30 minutes? I’ll set a short Huddle and share a playbook.

—Marissa
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood POC - intermittent 503s during high-concurrency tests

I’m available. Adding a few field-observation data points:
- We’ve seen similar failures when prefix KV cache grows >1.2GB on rdx-large under continuous batching. The runtime currently uses eager KV retention for streaming sessions which increases memory pressure.
- Quick check: Elena, can you share the average request tokens + prompt size for the failing period? The logs include request_id but not token counts.

Proposed immediate plan (30-min bridge):
1) Replicate on a controlled burst (we’ll run a synthetic load from our side).
2) If repro, switch OptiMed to non-streaming and set batch_max_tokens lower (suggest 256) — this is a config toggle on your SDK snippet.
3) If that fails, we’ll roll a runtime patch to change KV retention to adaptive for the session (short-lived change, rollbackable).

I’ll open SUP-1729 and capture artifacts.

—Karthik
Field Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T16:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood POC - intermittent 503s during high-concurrency tests

I’ll join the bridge. From the runtime side:
- Runtime logs show a short spike of OOM-retries in the serving engine for node pool pool-a (gpu-a100-pps). Those retries can manifest as 503s when the scheduler preempts requests to reclaim memory.
- Short-term runtime knob: enable "stream_low_mem_mode" which disables eager KV retention and serializes streaming chunks. It increases latency slightly but prevents preemptive OOM. I can enable it per-customer for the demo.
- Longer-term: we should add an adaptive batching heuristic that considers current KV cache size; I’ll start a design doc.

Action items from runtime:
- Dev: enable stream_low_mem_mode for OptiMed on their POC tenancy for the demo.
- Karthik: provide token-size stats so we can tune batch_max_tokens.
- Marissa: confirm with OptiMed whether disabling streaming for demo is acceptable if we need to fall back.

—Dev
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@optimed.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-12T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood POC - intermittent 503s during high-concurrency tests

Elena — quick update from the bridge:
- Short-term: we can enable a per-tenant runtime flag (stream_low_mem_mode) for the Friday demo window. That will reduce 503 risk but may add ~50-120ms p90 latency.
- Alternate: drop streaming and reduce batch_max_tokens to 256; this is simpler and removes the runtime change.
- Action required from you: send average token counts for the problematic window (approx per-request tokens + expected output tokens). Also confirm whether streamed partial responses are a hard requirement for the demo.

If OptiMed wants us to avoid any runtime changes, choose option 2 and we’ll help patch the SDK sample in your repo. If you prefer runtime opt-in, we’ll schedule the enable and monitoring for Friday.

Thanks — I’ll attach the short playbook we used on the bridge (bridging-playbook-v1.pdf).

—Marissa

--- Attachment: bridging-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook, 6 pages)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@optimed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: OptiMed Platform Team <infra@optimed.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T18:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood POC - intermittent 503s during high-concurrency tests

Thanks all — quick answers after internal check:
- Average incoming prompt tokens (per request): 420 tokens. Expected model output tokens: ~120 tokens.
- Streaming is nice-to-have but not required for the demo; we can fall back to non-streaming if it stabilizes the system.
- OptiMed prefers we avoid runtime flags for the initial demo. Please send the SDK snippet we should use with batch_max_tokens=256 and the truncated system prompt.

Marissa — can you push the SDK example to our shared drive link and I’ll confirm with our infra team? Also, please include the rollback steps if we see regressions after the change.

Appreciate the rapid support.
Elena
